static_traits.name: Chen Gerui
static_traits.family_status: Husband works in the telecommunications industry; has two daughters
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends and her husband as support, but has not yet communicated deeply with them about driving anxiety; relationship tension due to assumptions about cousins' views
static_traits.medical_history: No similar problems before; no prior psychotherapy experience; No major physical illness

basic_info.main_problem: I feel frustrated and anxious when driving, which affects my daily life and causes distress.
basic_info.core_demands: The increasingly severe driving anxiety has become hard to bear, so I seek counseling to effectively handle and manage this problem.
growth_experiences: A 'near-accident' experience while driving a few months ago (almost a collision), followed by gradually emerging driving-related significant anxiety and avoidance: more tense during crowded or high-traffic times, feeling out of control especially when merging on highways or encountering temporary detours; tried listening to soothing music and deep breathing, slightly helpful but overall anxiety persists.

core_beliefs: I am not accepted by others(especially worrying about being disliked by relatives)
I am unable to cope with unpredictable driving situations; something could go wrong at any time

special_situations.event: Planning to go out with cousins or thinking about being with them
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I act showy, they will surely dislike me and exclude me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing contact with relatives, repressing genuine self-expression to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will hate being with me

special_situations.event: Needs to drive on crowded or high-traffic roads
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once traffic gets congested or complex situations arise, I am unable to handle it and an accident may happen
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding rush hours and congested roads, listening to soothing music while driving, doing deep breathing to try to reduce anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot handle it; something terrible will happen

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as I need to merge, I will lose control or make a serious mistake
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to choose routes that do not require merging or traveling during less busy times
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I definitely cannot manage it; something will go wrong

special_situations.event: Encountering a temporary detour or sudden route change
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once unpredictable changes occur, I have no control over driving at all
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding unfamiliar routes, preferring predictable roads and times
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will completely lose control and not know what to do

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and understood by close people (husband, relatives) and to gain a sense of safety and control in driving and in life
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and looked down upon; fearing losing control and encountering danger in unpredictable situations
defense_goal: Reducing anxiety and shame by avoiding high-risk driving situations and repressing self-expression, maintaining surface safety and self-esteem

object_relations.self_representation: A vulnerable person who is judged and easily rejected
object_relations.linking_affect: Anxiety, shame, fear of being rejected

object_relations.self_representation: A vulnerable person easily hurt by fear of being slighted
object_relations.object_representation: A partner who may criticize or look down on them

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests communicating with her husband about driving anxiety to seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client worries her husband will think she cannot even handle 'basic driving' and thus look down on her (projecting inner shame and worry onto her husband)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'not wanting to be looked down upon' in a hesitant, cautious tone; suggesting postponing communication or displacing the topic onto practical difficulties.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor guides her to view driving risks and anxiety from a more balanced perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client uses 'roads are unpredictable' as a reason, emphasizing rational-level uncontrollability, thereby downplaying emotional experiences and bodily feelings
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Stating 'uncontrollability' in an objective, calm tone; reducing description of and dwelling on emotions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about why he avoids crowded road sections, merging, or detours
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client interprets all avoidance behaviors as 'for safety', rationalizing anxiety and fear as necessary caution
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes 'caution is necessary', mainly with declarative sentences and chains of reasons, weakening acknowledgment of inner fear.

manifestations: Feeling that roads are unpredictable while driving, experiencing a sense of losing control
Intense powerlessness and tension when encountering merging and detours
outcomes: Anxiety intensified and avoidance of driving situations
Daily affairs affected; increased stress in life

manifestations: Presuming cousins will dislike oneself, relationships strained as a result
Feeling embarrassed and ashamed about expressing vulnerability to husband and seeking support
outcomes: Social avoidance; support system not yet fully activated
Enhanced self-denial and fear of being rejected

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing relatives will dislike oneself and avoiding contact
Worrying her husband will look down on her, thus unwilling to express true feelings

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, including excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, being overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Internalizing the self-demand of 'not even being able to drive' as shame
Repeatedly self-censoring before expressing needs and seeking support, remaining indecisive

positive_force: Has a social support network of the husband and several close friends
Has tried self-regulation strategies such as soothing music and deep breathing
Actively seeks psychological counseling, with willingness to change
negative_force: A thinking pattern of catastrophizing and predicting the futureReinforcementFear
Mind reading and overgeneralization lead to social avoidance and relationship tension
Avoidance of driving situations maintains the anxiety cycle
Shame and worry about being looked down on hinder seeking help from intimate relationships

target_behavior.behavior: High anxiety and avoidance when driving
antecedent: Encountering a temporary detour or sudden route change
target_behavior.core_reason: The 'near-accident' experience a few months ago triggered catastrophic and out-of-control beliefs about driving dangers, reinforcing fear of uncertainty
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential danger and loss of control; short-term relief of anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Avoiding certain driving scenarios leads to decreased efficiency in errands and daily affairs, increased stress in overall life, and tense emotions after returning home affecting family atmosphere

antecedent: Planning a gathering with relatives or thinking about being with them
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by mind reading and overgeneralization about others' evaluations and the inner core belief of 'I am not accepted'
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the risk of being rejected and shame, maintaining self-protection
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, reduced sources of support, feelings of loneliness and worsened self-negation
